passages.original: Valentinianus ventus imminentem jam cervicibus suis tyrannum, ad Theodosium confugit. e [Honorius et Arcadius XXXII, CCCC. Theodosius et Joannes xxv et XXII. Valentinianus et Martianus III, CCCC, XXV]. Augustinus Mediolani rhetoricam apprime docens, .omissis scholis, ad .fidem rectam convertitur, cum ante Manichaeus fuisset.
passages.english: Valentinian, fearing the tyrant who was now pressing upon his neck, fled to Theodosius. [Honorius and Arcadius 32, 400. Theodosius and John 25 and 22. Valentinian and Marcian 3, 400, 25.] Augustine, who was teaching rhetoric with great distinction at Milan, gave up his school and was converted to the right faith, though he had previously been a Manichaean.
passages.notes: "ventus" is evidently a scanning error for "veritus" (fearing), and the text is translated so. The stray "e" before the bracket is taken as a footnote mark and omitted. The bracketed list of names and numerals appears to be an intrusive chronological or reckoning note, perhaps a gloss or a misplaced table entry. Its meaning is unclear, and it is rendered literally with the numerals transcribed. The dots before "omissis" and "fidem" are scanning artefacts.

passages.original: Augustinus plurima libris a innumeris disserit.
passages.english: Augustine discusses a great many matters in innumerable books.
passages.notes: The stray "a" after "libris" is taken as a footnote mark and omitted.
